hook.text: 'Google' was a noun—then overnight people started to 'google' things. No affix needed.

buildup.text: Conversion (or zero derivation) changes a word's part of speech without any visible change.

discovery.text: English is rich in conversion: 'run' (verb) → 'a run' (noun); 'clean' (adjective) → 'clean' (verb).

twist.text: Highly inflected languages like Russian rarely allow conversion—word forms are too fixed.

climax.text: Conversion thrives in English because English has so few inflectional endings to get in the way.

punchline.text: Same word, new job—no changes required.

quiz.question: What is conversion in morphology?
options: Changing a word's part of speech without adding affixes
